strings.name: Jeff Koons
strings.summary: Koons trained in painting and worked in New York finance before making sculptures from everyday symbols such as vacuum cleaners, toys and balloon animals. He organizes specialist fabrication teams, bringing craft, replication and commodity value into contemporary art debate, with work shown in major museums. His commercialization and appropriation divide critics, and French copyright litigation has found infringement in his use of others’ imagery.
strings.coverageNote: Selected milestones verifiable through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Through everyday consumer symbols and large sculptures, he examines popular imagery, commodities and artistic value, exercising broad influence in international contemporary art.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: BFA, Maryland Institute College of Art (1976); also studied at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Everyday objects and sculpture
strings.highlights.h1.text: Transforms household objects and toy imagery into sculpture, examining popular taste, replication and commodity culture.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Debating artistic value
strings.highlights.h2.text: Large sculptures and specialized fabrication influence international art debate while raising disputes about commercialization and appropriation.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Cultural diplomacy award
strings.timeline.t1.text: His official biography records receipt of the Meridian Cultural Diplomacy Award in Washington.
strings.timeline.t2.title: French copyright ruling upheld
strings.timeline.t2.text: The Paris Court of Appeal upheld the infringement ruling over Fait d’hiver and its use of advertising imagery.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Whitney retrospective
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Whitney Museum surveyed his different series and long artistic career in a retrospective.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Creates Puppy
strings.timeline.t4.text: Combined horticulture, public display and a popular image in a monumental floral sculpture.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Introduces Banality
strings.timeline.t5.text: Used porcelain, wood sculpture and other forms to address popular figures and decorative imagery.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Creates Rabbit
strings.timeline.t6.text: Transformed an inflatable toy into stainless steel, producing one of his signature sculptures.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Early New York presentation
strings.timeline.t7.text: Displayed household-object installations in a New Museum window, developing an early series.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes art degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Graduated from the Maryland Institute College of Art, then moved to New York.
